A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same utility-focused annotation study despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. V1 has no appendices; v3's Appendices A–G are included in the comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original annotation analyses, retriever-training experiments, and retrieval and RAG results on MS MARCO and out-of-domain datasets.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds Contriever evaluations, NQ annotation and training, and further empirical analyses in its appendices.

M1.justification: The relevance selection, pseudo-answer generation, utility selection/ranking, positive sampling, and curriculum-learning procedures are retained. SumMargLH renames Disj-InfoNCE while preserving its summed-positive objective. The additional corpus and backbone experiments do not establish a revised core algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds annotation and retriever training on NQ using candidates from BM25 and MS MARCO-trained retrievers. V1 used NQ only for out-of-domain evaluation. The existing MS MARCO, TREC DL, BEIR, and RAG evaluation coverage remains, making this a focused extension of training and annotation coverage.

E2.justification: REPLUG (Human), which first trained on human labels and then optimized with REPLUG labels, disappears from the corresponding retrieval, RAG, and BEIR comparisons. Human, REPLUG, and the curriculum-learning comparators remain. The added Contriever experiments reuse the annotation comparator set.

E3.justification: V3 adds Contriever evaluations and protocols for NQ training with Qwen3-32B and First1LH/SumMargLH, human-positive inclusion/exclusion controls, and top-1 versus top-5 RAG evaluation. Existing training budgets remain unchanged. V3 explicitly defines Hybrid Test as a union of human and GPT positives; v1's less explicit description and identical shared scores leave unresolved whether this represents relabeling or clarification.

E4.justification: V3 adds human-positive dependence tests during retriever training (Tables 7–8), RAG context-size analysis (Table 13), and loss comparisons across positive-count thresholds (Table 16). Section 3.2 also newly reports manual inspection of approximately 200 annotations. Earlier positive-sampling analyses are retained in Appendix B.2 and Table 11.

E5.justification: Appendix D.2 newly discloses a single training run using a default random seed, without giving its numerical value. V1 did not report run or seed information. The paired two-sided t-tests at p < 0.05 and exclusion of corpus-level BLEU from significance testing are retained; no additional runs or uncertainty intervals are established.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial Contriever, NQ, and controlled-analysis results. For example, Table 12 reports Contriever BEIR averages of 42.3 for UtilSel and 39.2 for Human. Matching RetroMAE scores largely persist, including UtilSel's 35.3 MS MARCO MRR@10. REPLUG (Human) rows and several recall cutoffs disappear. Table 17 corrects v1's swapped table timings to 53 hours for UtilSel and 70+ for REPLUG.

T1.justification: V1 Equation 5 incorrectly simplifies Equation 4's sum of log probabilities, omitting the required denominator power. V3 Equation 3 uses a product of normalized probabilities, removing that error. The proposed summed-positive objective and background dense-retrieval and KL formulas otherwise remain equivalent; no new proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain: utility annotations improve out-of-domain generalization, perform worse alone on in-domain evaluation, and can match full human supervision when combined with 20% human labels through curriculum learning. Full human-label integration can improve performance further. Reorganized research questions and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies REPLUG's poor performance by explaining its static adaptation, and discusses reproduction differences involving hard negatives, pretraining corpora, and pooling. It adds interpretations of human-positive dependence, context-size degradation, and loss effectiveness as positive counts change. Its limitations discussion extends v1's annotation-pool caveat, although the exclusion experiment only removes human positives during retriever training.

D1.justification: V3 supplies complete conversational annotation prompts, threshold-rounding rules, more explicit sampling details, NQ evaluation-query filtering, the BERT-Score model, and static-negative and pooling disclosures. It changes the stated repository address and explicitly includes data in its release statement. Conversely, v1's PyTorch/Transformers versions and temperature setting are omitted.

R1.justification: Literature coverage is substantially refocused: v1's historical relevance/utility discussion and non-IR annotation examples are removed, while neural and direct-LLM retrieval work is added, including Li et al., Springer et al., and Zhang et al. 2025. Appendix E.3 adds contextual comparisons with published retriever results. The central positioning around training-time utility annotation remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Three research-question groups become four, loss terminology changes, and results are organized by retrieval versus RAG. Preliminary material, implementation details, sampling analyses, and costs move into appendices. Separate limitations and ethics sections are introduced.

P2.justification: V3 changes the document template and author layout, redraws Figure 1, and clarifies Figure 2's axes. Figure 3 combines the earlier curriculum-learning MRR and threshold plots while dropping the curriculum-learning recall panel. Table 2 gains parallel backbone columns, the ablation table is split, and new appendix tables and full-prompt figures substantially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: V1's automation evidence relied on MS MARCO annotation and one retriever backbone. V3 substantially strengthens it through Contriever validation, NQ training with retrieved candidate pools, and targeted dependence analyses. Complete prompts, clearer baseline disclosures, and the joint-loss correction also improve reproducibility and interpretation. Some comparator coverage and implementation details are lost, and training-only exclusion does not eliminate human positives from annotation inputs, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantive gains.
